resumen: Hanging from a pull-up bar, you raise the straight legs to horizontal or higher, without swinging. One of the most demanding abdominal exercises.
ejecucion: Hang from a pull-up bar with your hands shoulder-width apart and your arms straight.
Brace your abs and glutes so your body does not swing.
Raise your straight legs to horizontal, or higher if you can, tilting your pelvis up.
Lower them under control, without letting your body swing at the bottom.
If you cannot raise them without swinging, start with your knees bent.
matices: In a study of fourteen men, the straight-leg version was, of the exercises measured, the most demanding for the abdominal wall: the rectus abdominis went beyond its reference maximal-contraction test (over 130 %) and the external oblique reached 88 %. It also loaded the spine with about 3000 N of compression, more than the body saw, which is worth bearing in mind with low back discomfort.

fuentes.titulo: Muscle activity and spine load during anterior chain whole body linkage exercises: the body saw, hanging leg raise and walkout from a push-up
fuentes.autor: McGill, Andersen and Cannon, J Sports Sci, 2015
